summary.text: 老 is interpreted in its oracle form as a bent, long-haired person holding a staff. It commonly means “old” or “aged”; the earliest cited oracle-bone use is a place name, whose relation to that meaning is unresolved.

formation.text: Pictographic: the oracle form is interpreted as the whole image of a bent, long-haired person holding a staff. A later Shuowen analysis separately parses 人、毛、匕 and explains the graph through whitening hair; it does not confirm the oracle form’s origin.

components.text: The oracle-form interpretation treats 老 as one picture: a bent, long-haired person holding a staff. Separately, the later Shuowen analysis parses 人、毛、匕 and explains the form through whitening hair; it is not a breakdown of the oracle picture.

history.text: The oracle-form account identifies 丨 as the staff; bronze forms render the staff in a 匕-like shape, sometimes written 止. Later upper-part forms vary, and one Spring and Autumn variant may use 由 as a phonetic element. That proposal concerns a later form, not the original construction.

uncertainties.text: The earliest cited oracle-bone use is a place name, with no established link to “old” and no absolute date for that instance. Reported bronze and Warring States uses do not establish a complete chronology.

The later Shuowen analysis parses 人、毛、匕. Duan Yucai offers a different reading of the seal form, deriving it from 毛匕 without treating 人 as a separate element. Neither confirms the oracle graph’s formation.

senses.text: The earliest cited oracle-bone instance uses 老 as a place name; it attests that use, not the lexical meaning “old.”

senses.period: bronze inscriptions; absolute dates not supplied here
senses.text: Reported bronze examples use 老 for an elderly person and as an adjective meaning “old.”

senses.gloss: father, written with 老 for 考
senses.period: bronze inscriptions; absolute dates not supplied here
senses.text: Bronze examples reportedly use 老 to write 考 “father.” Whether this was a semantic development or a writing substitution is unresolved.
The common current meaning is “old” or “aged.”
“Experienced” is also recorded as a current sense; its development is undated here.

limitations.text: The place-name, elderly-person, adjective, and father uses do not establish a chronological semantic chain. The reciprocal gloss of 老 and 考 and the traditional 轉注 account are historical interpretations, not proof of how these senses developed.

items.caption: Seal-script form of 老, shown here as a modern vector reconstruction. It provides a later graphic form to compare with the reported oracle and bronze forms.
items.alt: Black seal-script character 老 on a white background, with a broad branching upper section above a long, curved lower stroke.
items.selection_reason: The identified seal-script form gives a useful visual comparison for the character’s graphic history; its modern reconstruction should not be mistaken for an ancient artifact.
